fields.places[].name: read: a place the settings pass chose for at least one passage
fields.people[]: read: names the reader verified, merged into one person by the entity pass; `as` says why each counts: a name, a description the book writes with a capital (title), or a named person's relation
fields.passages[].place: read: where the passage takes place (settings pass), with its basis and any flags
fields.passages[].at: code: the place to stand on; a passage set 'unclear' or 'elsewhere' keeps the place before it
fields.passages[].tension, .warmth: read: 0-10, with the reader's one-sentence reason and cited sentences in .tone
fields.passages[].people: read: persons with a verified character fact in this passage, and what they are called here
fields.passages[].meetings, .objects, .events: read: verified facts of those types, each with its fact id and spans
fields.sentences.start, .end: code: exact offsets of the sentence in the source file
fields.sentences.speech: code: 1 if any of the sentence lies inside quotation marks
fields.sentences.people: code: persons named in the sentence, by a name the reader verified for them in this passage, or by a name it only ever verified for one person in the whole book; pronouns are not resolved, so 'she' names nobody
fields.sentences.places: code: places named in the sentence, by a name in the book's own gazetteer
fields.sentences.cited: code: how many accepted facts cite this sentence
fields.sentences.feeling, .pace: read: the first reading's labels for the sentence. feeling 0 neither, 1 warm, 2 cold; pace 0 calm, 1 tense; -1 where the reading has no usable answer
fields.sentences.feeling_b, .pace_b: read: the same labels from the second reading, which asks in other words
fields.chapters[]: code: passages grouped by chapter; tension is the highest in the chapter, warmth the mean
